playbookOutputs: Income statement for the sole proprietorship (business section of the ITR12)
Tax computation showing liability or refund
playbookCommonFailures: Bank statements incomplete so the year's income cannot be reconstructed; SARS third-party data shows more income than declared
Private expenses (groceries, personal vehicle, home bond) claimed as business expenses
Motor vehicle costs claimed without a logbook
Client is a registered VAT vendor or has employees and the trade figures do not reconcile to VAT201/EMP201 already filed
Client should have been a provisional taxpayer and faces underestimation penalties on assessment

informationToProvide.label: Company Name
informationToProvide.aiHint: Trading name of the sole proprietorship AND the full name of the individual owner — the taxpayer is the individual, the business has no separate tax number.

informationToProvide.label: Copy of your South African ID document or passport
informationToProvide.aiHint: ID book / smart ID (both sides) or passport of the individual owner.

informationToProvide.label: Proof of all income received (e.g., invoices, bank statements, IRP5s/IT3(a)s for any employment)
informationToProvide.aiHint: Business bank statements for the full tax year (1 March – end Feb) plus invoices or a sales report; IRP5/IT3(a) for any salaried employment alongside the trade.

informationToProvide.label: Records of all business expenses (e.g., receipts, bank statements, vehicle logbook if applicable)
informationToProvide.aiHint: Receipts/invoices or an expense listing by category; vehicle logbook if motor expenses are claimed; asset list with cost and purchase date for wear-and-tear. Private expenses paid from the business account must be identified.

informationToProvide.label: Any other relevant tax documents (e.g., medical aid certificates, retirement annuity certificates)
informationToProvide.aiHint: Medical scheme certificate, RA certificate, IT3(b) interest certificates for the owner personally.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Collect eFiling access, income records and expense records
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Bank statements for the full tax year, income evidence, expense records and personal certificates uploaded
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Ask for the full tax year (1 March to end February) of business bank statements first — they are the backbone of the income statement. Then expense records by category, a logbook if a vehicle is used, and personal certificates (IRP5, medical, RA). Confirm whether the client is a VAT vendor or employer so the figures can be reconciled. Do not promise a turnaround shorter than 3–5 working days.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Verify completeness of records
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: No statement gaps in the year; expense evidence supports each category; logbook compliant if vehicle claimed
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: The taxpayer is the individual; the trade is reported in the "Local business, trade and professional income" section of the ITR12, there is no separate business tax number. Check statement continuity (closing balance = next opening balance). Flag deposits that look like loans/transfers versus sales. Flag private spend.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Compile income statement and tax computation
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Income statement by ITR12 expense category and tax computation reviewed by Kevin
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Build the income statement in the AI Accountant module from the bank statements and records: turnover, cost of sales, expense categories matching the ITR12 business schedule, wear-and-tear per SARS Interpretation Note 47 write-off periods, home office apportionment, motor expenses per logbook business %. Add salary/interest/medical/RA at the personal level. Assessed loss ring-fencing (s20A) is Kevin's call. ⚠ verify current rebates, thresholds and IN47 periods.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Draft tax computation and handoff sheet
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Every ITR12 business-section field and personal field listed with its value and source
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Include the business schedule totals (turnover, cost of sales, each expense line, net profit/loss), balance sheet fields if SARS requires them for the turnover band, and personal items. Note whether the client is a provisional taxpayer and any IRP6 payments already made (they appear on the assessment).

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Complete and submit the ITR12 with business schedule on eFiling
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: ITR12 submitted; confirmation and summary screenshot saved
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Returns Issued → ITR12 → tax year. In the wizard answer YES to "Did you receive income from local business, trade or profession" and set the number of trades. Fill the business schedule from the handoff sheet; the agent drives to the summary, Kevin checks and presses Submit. eFiling login from a new device/IP triggers an OTP to the taxpayer's registered cell/email: pause, raise an otpRequest on the portal job via the OTP relay (Kevin, or the client through the Communication History link if allowed), 10-minute timeout then fail cleanly and reschedule. Never store OTPs. If a CAPTCHA appears, fall back to hand-off mode with the handoff sheet. Prefer filing from our practitioner profile if the taxpayer is already linked as a client; otherwise use the client's own login. If the taxpayer is not registered for the tax type on eFiling, stop and raise a proposal — do not activate tax types without Kevin.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Wait for ITA34 and handle verification
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: ITA34 received, or verification documents uploaded and outcome received
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Sole-prop returns with a loss or large expenses are often verified. If SARS asks for supporting documents, propose the bundle (income statement, bank statements, expense evidence, logbook) for Kevin to approve, then upload via eFiling within the window on the letter (⚠ verify: 21 business days).

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Deliver ITA34, income statement and outcome note
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: ITA34, computation and plain-English note posted to Communication History
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Explain the outcome and the payment due date on the ITA34. If the client is not yet a provisional taxpayer but the trade profit means they should be, explain IRP6 in plain terms and offer the provisional tax service. No deadline threats.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Final sign-off
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Kevin confirms the order can be completed
